title: “I have much more to say to you, more than you can now bear.  But when he, the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak on his own; he will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is yet to come. He will glorify me because it is from me that he will receive what he will make known to you. All that belongs to the Father is mine. That is why I said the Spirit will receive from me what he will make known to you.”
devotional:
The second new name Jesus gives to the Holy Spirit is parakletos. There has been a lot of debate about why Jesus used this word to describe the Holy Spirit at this time?  Paraklētos is variously translated as the "Comforter" (KJV), "Counsellor" (NIV, RSV), "Advocate" (NRSV), "Helper" (ESV). It can't be easily translated into English with one word that adequately covers its breadth of meaning. But there is a question that might help us understand this ministry of the Spirit.

When we have to face painful truths about ourselves, and demanding life- changing truths about God, what do we need? When we are wrestling with uncomfortable truth about ourselves we need comfort. When we are struggling with demanding truth that God has brought into our lives that will require sacrifice and change, we need help. When truth challenges our ‘status quo’ we need counsel. The parakletos is God personally assisting us through the ministry of the Holy Spirit to come to terms with the truth and live with its consequences.

As Jesus spoke his last words to his disciples he knew that very soon they would be feeling very frightened and insecure without Him, so he knew that they would need to know the ongoing help of the Spirit to encourage them to live in truth about themselves and about God.

The way the Spirit helps us is that He draws close to us bringing assurance and hope and gives us courage to face the things we want to run from and hide.
prayer: Father thank you that the Spirit who confronts with the truth, is the same Spirit who comforts us.
